The Co/FeCo/NPC-3 nanocomposite achieved an optimal reflection loss of -48.4 dB and an effective absorption bandwidth of 5.23 GHz in the X-band at a thickness of 3.4 mm.
By optimizing the thickness, the Co/FeCo/NPC-3 nanocomposite exhibited an optimal reflection loss of -40.30 dB at 5.68 GHz in the C-band.
The Co/FeCo/NPC-3 nanocomposite had the highest BET surface area of 590.13 m²/g among the samples.
The XRD and XPS analyses confirmed the presence of both metallic Co and FeCo alloy phases in the nanocomposites.
Nitrogen doping created defects and dipole polarization centers, while the Co/FeCo nanoparticles enhanced impedance matching and introduced magnetic loss mechanisms.
The nanocomposites exhibited multiple polarization relaxation processes, including interfacial polarization and dipole polarization.

Increasing the Fe and Co content in the nanocomposites enhanced the balance between dielectric and magnetic properties, leading to improved impedance matching and overall microwave absorption performance.
The coatings based on the Co/FeCo/NPC-3 nanocomposite demonstrated a radar cross-section reduction of up to 20.82 dBm².
The magnetic loss mechanisms in the nanocomposites included exchange resonance and eddy current effects.

The attenuation coefficient (α) of the Co/FeCo/NPC-2 and Co/FeCo/NPC-3 nanocomposites was higher than that of the Co/FeCo/NPC-1 nanocomposite, indicating a better ability to attenuate electromagnetic waves.
The saturation magnetization (Ms) of the Co/FeCo/NPC-3 nanocomposite was 149.3 emu/g, significantly higher than the other nanocomposites.
The coercivity (Hc) values for the Co/FeCo/NPC nanocomposites ranged from 18.6 to 24.9 Oe.
The dielectric loss tangent (tanδε) and imaginary permittivity (ε″) of the nanocomposites increased with rising FeCo content, indicating enhanced interfacial polarization.
The real part of the complex permeability (μ′) of the nanocomposites exhibited a declining trend with increasing frequency due to magnetic relaxation effects.
The eddy current loss was a dominant magnetic loss mechanism at frequencies greater than 14 GHz for all the nanocomposites.
